title: Store health
purpose: When I cannot be sure the store is taking orders and getting paid, open Store health to know it is open, checkout works and every order is paid and delivered, so no sale is lost to something broken nobody saw.
fires: The customer email that says 'your checkout is broken', the midnight check on the orders app, the developer called in after the damage, the launch spreadsheet of ticked boxes, and the habit of not looking until sales dip.
not_for: A brand whose platform partner or agency already runs round-the-clock monitoring with a named owner and a weekly report the founder reads and trusts.

jobs.job: When the store or checkout stops taking orders at 9 pm on a Saturday or while I sleep, tell me within minutes, so I do not keep paying for ads that send shoppers who cannot buy
jobs.circumstance: Saturday evening, ads are spending, the payment step throws an error, and nobody is looking

progress.functional: know within minutes that orders stopped, and where in the path it breaks
progress.emotional: sleep without checking the orders app on my phone
progress.social: be the one who knew first, not the customer who emailed

jobs.hire_today: nothing; a customer email or a strangely quiet sales day is the alarm
jobs.fire: checking the orders app at night, and the customer email as the alarm

forces.push: a 3 hour checkout fault on a Saturday cost a day of sales
forces.pull: a test order through the path every few minutes, and a call when it fails
forces.habit: the platform is supposed to just work
forces.anxiety: what if it wakes me for false alarms

jobs.little_hire: silent until it matters; a glance each morning

watch.metric: minutes from checkout breaking to someone being told, per incident, and hours with no orders in normal trading hours, 30 days
watch.source: synthetic checkout test log and Shopify orders

drives.metric: revenue lost to downtime, 30 days (orders expected minus orders taken in the gap, times average order value)

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a checkout fault ran 3 hours before a customer emailed. After: an alert within 5 minutes and a fix in under 1 hour.
jobs.not_for: a store doing a few orders a week, where hours without an order are normal and tell you nothing

jobs.job: When a shopper picks Apple Pay, PayPal or a card and the payment fails, tell me which method broke, so I stop losing buyers at the very last step
jobs.circumstance: Apple Pay orders dropped after a checkout app update last week and nobody noticed

progress.functional: each payment method completes a real order, checked on a schedule
progress.emotional: trust that every button on checkout works

jobs.hire_today: a test order at launch, then nothing

forces.push: Apple Pay completes 41 percent of attempts against 78 percent for cards
forces.pull: completion by payment method, with a flag when one falls behind
forces.habit: if cards work, everything works
forces.anxiety: what if test orders cost money or muddy the numbers

jobs.little_hire: weekly, and after any checkout or app change

watch.metric: checkout completion rate by payment method, 7 days
watch.source: Shopify checkouts and orders by payment gateway

drives.metric: checkout to order rate, 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: Apple Pay 41 percent against 78 percent for cards. After: every method within 5 points, tested weekly with a real order.
jobs.not_for: a store with one payment method on a hosted checkout it cannot change

jobs.job: When a developer, an agency or I change the theme or add an app, tell me the next morning if add to cart, the cart or a discount code broke, so I do not lose a week of sales blaming the ads
jobs.circumstance: An upsell app went in on Tuesday; by Friday sales are down and the agency says it is the ads

progress.functional: each change logged and followed by a check of browse, cart, discount and checkout
progress.emotional: stop the week of guessing
progress.social: settle the argument with the agency using facts

jobs.hire_today: a developer who checks when told something is wrong
jobs.fire: finding breaks from a sales dip

forces.push: a discount code broke for 4 days after an app update
forces.pull: a change log with a before and after on the steps that matter, and the change named
forces.habit: changes go live and everyone moves on
forces.anxiety: what if it flags every tiny theme tweak

watch.metric: add to cart rate and checkout start rate, the day after each change against the 14 day average
watch.source: Shopify and GA4 funnel, with the store change log

drives.metric: days a break stays live before it is found, per incident

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a broken discount code ran 4 days. After: flagged the next morning and rolled back the same day.
jobs.not_for: a store that has not changed its theme or apps in months

jobs.job: When shoppers reach checkout and leave, help me remove the settings that make them quit, like a forced account or 11 fields, so I turn more of the carts I paid for into orders
jobs.circumstance: Checkout completion is 52 percent, and the settings were chosen at launch 2 years ago

progress.functional: checkout has guest checkout, few fields and express wallets first
progress.emotional: stop wondering if checkout itself is the leak

jobs.hire_today: the developer's setup at launch, then nothing

forces.push: half of checkouts do not finish
forces.pull: the exact settings to change, each one small and quick
forces.habit: we set it up once
forces.anxiety: what if a change lowers order value or lets in more fraud

jobs.little_hire: each quarter, and after a platform checkout update

watch.metric: checkout to order rate, mobile, 30 days

drives.metric: orders, 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 11 fields and a forced account; 52 percent complete. After: 7 fields, guest on, wallets first; 58 percent.
jobs.not_for: a store on a checkout it cannot configure

jobs.job: When orders sit unshipped, stuck on payment pending, a fraud hold or a failed sync to the warehouse, find them before the customer writes in, so I never forget a paid order
jobs.circumstance: Friday; 14 orders from Tuesday are still unshipped because a tag stopped them syncing to the warehouse

progress.functional: every paid order ships on time, and stuck ones are listed with the reason
progress.emotional: stop the fear of a forgotten order
progress.social: customers see a store that keeps its promises

jobs.hire_today: customer service, once the customer writes in

forces.push: stuck orders turn into refunds and 1 star reviews
forces.pull: a daily list of orders past their ship date, with why
forces.habit: the warehouse ships whatever it gets
forces.anxiety: what if the list fills up with normal preorders

watch.metric: paid orders not shipped past the promised ship date, count, daily

drives.metric: on time ship rate, 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 14 orders stuck 3 days before anyone saw. After: flagged within 24 hours; 0 stuck over 2 days.
jobs.not_for: a store where the platform and warehouse are one system and orders cannot stall between them

jobs.job: When a sale is set to go live at midnight, check that the prices, the code and the banner actually changed, so I do not stay up refreshing the store

jobs.hire_today: the founder, awake at midnight

forces.habit: I always check myself
forces.anxiety: what if the check says fine and it is not

watch.metric: minutes from scheduled promo start to confirmed live, per promo
watch.source: Shopify discounts and prices, plus a page check

drives.metric: promo day revenue against plan

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the founder checks by hand at midnight. After: confirmed within 5 minutes while the founder sleeps.
jobs.not_for: a store that never runs timed promos

jobs.job: When cash on delivery parcels keep coming back refused, stop the risky orders before they ship, so I do not pay shipping both ways for nothing (market option: reads unavailable for US stores)

progress.emotional: stop the feeling of shipping money away

jobs.hire_today: an ops lead calling buyers, or a cash on delivery confirmation tool

forces.anxiety: what if blocking cash on delivery loses real buyers

watch.metric: return to origin rate on cash on delivery orders, 30 days
watch.source: Shopify orders and courier delivery status

drives.metric: shipping cost lost on returned cash on delivery orders, 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 24 percent come back. After: 15 percent within 60 days.
jobs.not_for: any store without cash on delivery, which includes US stores by default

jobs.job: When the store is about to launch or relaunch, prove every step with a real order, a refund and a real email, so I do not send the first weeks of paid traffic to a broken store

progress.emotional: go live calm instead of crossing my fingers

jobs.fire: the ticked box with no proof behind it

forces.pull: a checklist that only turns green when a real order proves it
forces.habit: the agency says it is done
forces.anxiety: what if a test order shows up in the numbers or costs money

jobs.little_hire: each launch, relaunch or new market

watch.metric: launch steps verified by a real customer action, share of all steps

drives.metric: fault tickets in the first 14 days after launch

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 30 of 42 steps ticked, 12 proven. After: 42 of 42 proven before the password comes off.
jobs.not_for: a store that has been live for years with no relaunch planned

jobs.job: When the store shows stock the warehouse does not have, catch the gap before we sell it, so I do not have to cancel orders and collect bad reviews
jobs.circumstance: A best seller showed 40 in stock; the warehouse had 6; 34 orders got canceled

progress.functional: store stock matches warehouse stock, with gaps flagged by product
progress.emotional: stop the dread of cancel emails

jobs.hire_today: an ops lead with a spreadsheet, or the warehouse telling us late

forces.push: 2.4 percent of orders are canceled for no stock

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 2.4 percent of orders canceled for no stock. After: under 0.5 percent.
jobs.not_for: a made-to-order or print-on-demand store with no stock to count

jobs.job: When Black Friday, a product drop or a TV mention is coming, get the store ready to take the rush, so I do not watch checkout fail on the best sales day of the year

forces.anxiety: what if the freeze blocks a fix we need

watch.metric: checkout completion in peak hours against a normal day, percentage point drop

progress.social: pay suppliers and staff on time

watch.metric: payouts held, failed or late, value, 30 days
